say: Keep your sermons. I've heard them all and the god never answered.
If you serve a flame or a saint, walk the other way.
Flotsam taught me to fight. Nobody taught me to forgive.
Say what you want and leave off the praying.
Another believer with a blade. Good.
Your god sent you? Then he can come collect you himself.
Stand there and pray. I'll finish while you do.
I know your kind. Paladins cry loudest when the blade goes in.
There's a Flotsam woman who spits at the mention of Okran. Nobody in the bar there argues with her.
Reva, they call her. Trained by the ninjas, angry with everything holy.
Saw a woman walk out of a Holy Nation sermon mid-prayer once. Reva, somebody said. She did not look back.
Hire Reva and you hire a temper. The sword comes free with it.
Green fields and not one honest face. I hate this place.
Every tower here has a prayer on it.
I keep my hood up in Holy country.
Walls and gates. I like open ground better.
Stay close. The plains are theirs and we're walking food.
Cannibals are no worse than priests. At least they say what they want.
Watch the grass. They like to lie in it.
Every hunter has a game trail. Ours is the one with fewer bodies.
Wet and lawless. Finally a place that doesn't lie about it.
Nobody here asks about gods. I could live with that.
Mind the mud. Slavers hide behind it.
Mud and flies. It's honest, at least.
Dead land, dead gods. Suits me.
Nothing out here to pray to, thank everything.
Quiet. Too quiet for my taste, and I don't like quiet.
Dust and bones. Fine company for the faithless.
Slavers in every doorway. Don't look at them. Don't turn your back.
Empire city. Clean shoes, dirty hands.
I won't be sold here. Remember that if you meet a buyer.
Do not let the guards look at our hands.
Down. Stay down.
That one prayed. It didn't help.
Next one steps forward. I have time.
Check them. Quickly.
I've had worse from a priest's temper.
Up. Up. I'm not finished.
Don't stand over me. Fight.
Lucky hit. It won't happen twice.
Stop fussing. Just tie it off.
Fine. Thanks. Don't make it a thing.
Careful. That is my good arm.
Hm. Not bad hands. Keep them to yourself.
Don't ask me about my past. Ask me about the road.
I'll keep your back. In return, keep your faith to yourself.
Still here, still angry. Take it or leave it.
If a priest crosses us, let me speak first. Briefly.
Don't come closer than the sword reaches.
I sleep badly. Don't make it worse.
Flotsam taught me to keep walking.
You want something? Be quick about it.
Draw. I'd rather get it over with.
I've done worse than you to people I loved.
Come on, then. You won't be the one who haunts me.
I was hoping for someone who could hurt me.
There's a Flotsam woman who sleeps outside walls and never in the beds. Digna. She doesn't like to talk about why.
Digna fights like she's paying off something. The kind of debt coin doesn't clear.
Heard Digna left home with her family chasing her. Didn't say who came back.
Hire Digna and you won't hear her complain. You'll hear her wake up at night.
I sleep better with a wall at my back. There are no walls here.
If something comes out of the grass I will cut it. Do not stop me.
Quiet plains. They're never quiet.
I'm not afraid. I'm only awake.
My home was somewhere like this. I don't recommend remembering it.
Flat fields, long memory. Keep moving.
Priests, paladins, patrols. Say nothing.
If a priest speaks, I leave. Remember that.
Mud does not remember anything. I like that.
Nights here are loud. Good. Silence is worse.
Keep a watch tonight. I'll take the first.
A dry spot and a fire. That's all I want.
Nothing alive to remind me of anyone. Good.
Dead land. I can breathe here.
Walk on. Don't stop to look.
Even the wind is quiet here.
It gets quieter every time. Not better.
Done. Move on.
They fell like anyone else.
Leave them. I do not need to look.
Pain is easy. It's the nights that are hard.
Not done yet. Help me up.
Hold on. I have a lot left.
I've buried worse hurts. Help me up.
Thanks. Don't ask how I got the old scars.
Quickly. I do not like being still.
Good. Back on my feet.
Don't look at my scars.
I don't talk about my father. Ask about the sword if you must.
The road is easier than a bed. Don't ask me why.
I'll fight for you. That's all I'm offering.
I follow orders better than I follow advice.
Are there paladins behind you? Tell me honestly.
I move fast. If this goes wrong, I won't be here.
My sister said never touch a sword. I touch swords.
Keep your hand off my purse. I'm quick and I know the price.
Holy Nation? No? Then fight me fair. If yes, I fight mean.
Naevia taught me to run. I came back to fight.
You're slow. I'm not.
Slow down and let me look at you. Oh.
Pia, the girl from Flotsam, jumps at a paladin's shadow. She's also the fastest thing on two legs I've seen.
Her sister died fighting paladins. Pia goes quiet when you say the name Naevia.
Pia wants three thousand cats to go with you. Cheap, for how fast she is.
Pia left the Holy Nation behind. She still checks every door for white cloaks.
Paladins. Everywhere. Keep close and don't look at them.
This is the worst place for me.
I know these roads. I hoped never to again.
Okran forgive me. No, don't.
No paladins in the swamp. I love the swamp.
Mud slows you down but I am still faster.
Quiet here, which means someone is waiting.
I almost feel safe. Almost. Hush.
Things hide in the grass. I can outrun most.
Cannibals don't frighten me half as much as holy robes.
Watch the high ground. They like it.
Fast, fast. Don't trail behind.
Everyone buys everything here. Even me, probably.
Paid guards. Paid friends. Pay me too, ha.
Don't stop. Keep moving.
If anyone asks, I never said I was a ninja.
For Naevia!
Fast enough, thank you.
They never see me move.
One more for the list.
Ow! I was faster than that!
Up. Up. They are not done.
That was luck. Next time it isn't.
Ow! I'm usually faster, I swear!
Ow, ow. Gently!
Thank you. Truly. I owe you.
Fine, fine. Back to it.
You have steadier hands than I have luck.
Do you think I could be as good as Naevia? Don't answer that.
I keep looking for white cloaks.
Money is easy here and nowhere else.
Is it true you can buy nearly anything in the Cities? Even a sword for me?
If you deal in slaves, speak plainly now.
I carry a name I don't say aloud.
I used to belong somewhere. Now I belong to the road.
Do you hate slavers? Say yes. It will save us both trouble.
You trade in people. That's reason enough.
I've waited a long time for someone like you.
Draw your blade and I'll give you what she never got.
Your hands smell of chains. Mine will smell of you.
Hamut is on the road again. Lost his wife to slavers and the Anti-Slavers would not take him in.
If you see a Greenlander killing slavers with no word at all, that's Hamut.
A widower with a blade. Hamut will fight beside you free, if you hate slavery as he does.
Hamut thinks the world owes him an answer. He seeks it in slavers' blood.
Slavers all around. I want to kill every one.
This is where they sell people. Do not ask me to stay long.
Walk. Don't buy anything. Don't look at the cages.
Another town built on someone's back.
Mud, mosquitoes, and men worse than both.
The slavers came through here once. Maybe still do.
Keep your voice down. The reeds hear.
Smoke and reeds. A slaver's hiding place, if ever there was.
Tinfist used to hit camps like this. I wish he were here.
Watch the grass. They hunt like slavers do.
I won't be taken. Not again, not here.
Slaves fed to the grass. I wouldn't be the first.
Holy walls. Holy chains. Same difference.
The paladins sell people too, quietly.
Move on. I don't like this air.
I don't trust the clean white coats.
Slavers fall the same as anyone.
One less. There are always more.
Forever remember. Never forget.
She would have wanted it done properly.
Not yet. I have more to do.
Up. I won't rest while they live.
Get me on my feet.
Not here. I haven't found her yet.
Thank you. I don't forget a kindness.
My hands are steady. It's only my head.
Good. Back to it.
Much obliged. It's a long road.
Do you ever hear someone you lost? In the wind, I mean.
If we meet slavers, don't hold me back.
I'm glad to walk with you. I'm not good company.
If I ever stop looking, you'll know I'm gone.
Back in my day, strangers bowed. Never mind. What do you want?
My back is gone and my pride follows.
Know who I was? The White Ripper.
I carried a master's sword once. Now I carry my own bones.
Old I may be, fool. Come and see what the old can do.
A noble's sword never tired. I'm tired, but not that tired.
You'll tell your children you fought the White Ripper.
I can still cut you into three. The fourth part is tricky.
The White Ripper still walks. Bent like a cane now, but they say nobody fenced like him in the Cities.
Crumblejon, the old samurai. Complains about his back and could still cut you in half.
Nobles used him and dropped him. He walks a free road now, and grumbles every step.
If an old man offers you a fight, check his blade first. It might be Crumblejon's.
I remember being paraded down streets like this. I was a boy then.
The Empire changes nothing and the nobles everything.
Rest soon. My back says so.
The Cities crumble like me. Differently.
Swamp mud in my boots at my age. Disgraceful.
Is there a dry stone anywhere? My knees ask.
Quiet. Mosquitoes bite old men hardest.
Damp ruins a sword and an old man alike.
If they eat me, keep my beard. It's the only part worth keeping.
Teeth like theirs on bones like mine. They'll break a tooth.
Back in my youth I killed a dozen of them before breakfast.
If a cannibal eats me, chew slowly.
Quiet. Good place for an old man to rest.
Nothing lives here. Even the flies have retired.
Slow down. I'm not the horse.
These stones were fresh when I was young.
Not bad for a crumbling old man.
Back in my youth, this took half the time.
The blade remembers even if I don't.
Help an old man loot the dead.
Ah! My back! Help me up, damn you.
Not yet. I am old, not finished.
Easy! I'm antique.
Don't just stand there. Pick up an old man.
Rub the back while you're at it. No? Fine.
Thank you. My bones thank you less.
Good hands. Better than the nobles' physicians.
Careful with the spine. It's decades older than you.
Nobles are fickle as fish. Remember that before you serve any.
Is there a soft chair anywhere? I am asking, not demanding.
I follow a new master now. You. Try not to disappoint me.
I've done this for forty years. My knees say thirty-nine too many.
Come, sit, have a drink, have a story. What do you mean you are leaving?
Have you ever wrestled a gorillo? I have. Barehanded. Mostly.
Beware the talking cacti! They remember who owes them.
I know a legend. It sleeps in a cave. Don't ask me which.
You, with the face! Fight me! I'm old and I'm angry and I'm drunk!
I wrestled a gorillo. You're smaller.
You'll go in my legend. As the one who lost.
Old Hobbs will buy you a drink and talk until the rum is gone. Stories of banshees and talking cacti.
He swears he wrestled a gorillo with a bottle in his belly. Nobody has the heart to tell him the gorillo would have won.
Hobbs wants a partner for his wailing thing. If you ever go, take plenty of rum.
Mad as a hatter and kinder than most. Hobbs is the old man who talks to cacti and thanks them.
Wet! Lovely! Like a cave, but with sky.
I once heard a wail in a swamp like this. Or was that my knees?
Do not step in anything that moves. Or anything that does not.
I know a tale about cannibals. It ends with truffles.
Hungry folk out here. Offer them a story. They like stories. They like me.
Quiet now. The grass listens. It always has.
Sand, sand, sand. Somewhere under it, a banshee.
My Aunt Una crossed a desert once. She didn't mention it after.
Thirsty! Who is thirsty? Not me, I am drinking.
Water as far as you can see. I knew a man who drank it all.
The wailing thing sleeps near water, they say. Or sand.
Wet boots, wet legend. Good day.
Dead land. Dead cacti. I salute them.
A very old story lives here. I forget it.
No rum here. A tragedy for the ages.
Ha! Into the legend with you!
Ah, they don't fight like gorillos.
Quick, quick, loot them before the cacti come.
Another tale for the cave.
Ow! A scratch! A glorious scratch!
Put me down, I'm a legend, I get up myself!
Hm, rum helps. It does, it does.
Thank you, thank you. Do you want a drink for it?
Gentle, gentle! I'm an antique!
Bind it tight. A story is only as good as its teller.
Did I tell you about the wailing thing? Of course I did. Did I mention the truffles?
The best stories are the ones I invent halfway through.
You don't seem to mind an old fool. That's rare.
Hello! Are you travelling far? I'd love some company.
A fine road for an adventure, is it not? Or a funeral.
I'm not a settler. I like roads. Do you?
Anything worth seeing around here? I always ask.
I'd rather chat, but if you insist.
Sorry about this. Truly.
Alright, alright. Let us get it over with.
There's a woman who wanders. Riddly, her name. Wants an adventure, any adventure. Hire her and she's cheerful the whole way.
Friendly sword for hire. Riddly. Never settles, never complains, never turns down a road.
Met Riddly once. Said she was looking for someone to ask her along. Nobody had. Now I regret it.
A lone adventurer who actually smiles. Riddly. It's unsettling and nice.
Wet! Wonderful! I like new terrain.
If we find something that glows, can we look at it first?
Mud is just soft ground. That's the way I look at it.
Everyone says don't go here.
Hold your breath, step light. This should be fun.
The grass is very tall. That is concerning and exciting.
So many people to talk to!
This is the Empire? I expected statues.
Look at that gate. Imagine paying to walk through.
Sleek, black, dry. Dramatic. I approve.
Do the skeletons here take visitors? I'll ask.
Nothing grows here. I feel for the plants.
Water, water, everywhere. Don't drink the middle.
I wonder what lives down there. Should we ask?
Wet boots. Great fun, wet boots.
Right! That went well, I think.
Sorry! Truly. Search them though.
Another adventure behind us.
Nobody hurt? Besides them, I mean.
Ow, ow, that stings. I am fine!
Just a scratch. A big one.
Hold on, up we go!
Thank you! Truly. I owe you tea.
You're kind. Don't tell anyone.
Better. A bit better. Mostly.
Thank you for asking me along. Nobody does.
The road is better with company. I didn't know that before.
I like you. You don't talk much.
Don't step on the crabs.
Crabs are far better company than people.
I talk to crabs. They never lie to me.
Do you like crabs? If you say no, I'll walk faster.
Leave the crabs alone. And me.
I'm not fighting you. I'm just very angry.
You frighten me. That isn't wise of you.
Crab Town has a woman who prefers crabs to people. Lumi. Harmless unless you hurt a crab.
Lumi speaks to the crabs. They're said to listen. Don't ask me how I know.
Someone in Crab Town speaks fluent crab. I am not joking. Ask Lumi.
Lumi moved there because she dislikes crowds. Crab Town suits her. The crabs didn't object.
Muddy things with legs. Wonderful. Don't bother them.
I think that one waved. Hello!
Be gentle, please. This is their home.
So many shells! Careful where you step.
I could stay here and talk to them for years.
They're shy at first. Then not.
Cold and quiet. Not even a crab.
I don't like the fog.
Stay close. I'm frightened, but I won't run.
Do not leave me alone in this grass.
I am frightened. Do not tell the crabs.
If something bites, I'll hit it with my bag.
Oh! Oh, I did it. Don't look at me.
Sorry, sorry. It had to be done.
I hate this part. Search them, please.
Please, no crabs near the bodies.
Owww! That hurt!
Please don't leave me. I'll get up.
I'm fine. I'm fine. I'm not fine.
Thank you, thank you. You're very kind.
Is it bad? Don't tell me.
Better. Slightly. Thank you.
I know it's silly, loving crabs. Nobody ever stops me, though.
I am a poor fighter. I try.
You're patient with me. Thank you.
I'm a medic, not a fighter. Come to me hurt, not angry.
Have you got a sponsor? Research costs more than swords.
Don't touch my bag. The samples are fragile.
The nobles are as fickle as fish. I only trust my notes.
I have a scalpel and no patience. Back away.
I've taken apart worse than you.
You'll need a medic after this. I won't be it.
A young medic named Izumi wants a sponsor for her experiments. Smart as they come, and she knows it.
Izumi, the girl with the notes and the sharp tongue. Heals better than most doctors twice her age.
Hire her and she will lecture you the whole way. Cheaper than a bad bandage, though.
Heard a girl in the bar telling a noble that his research was nonsense. Izumi. Nobody argued.
Interesting. The water here's full of things I want to look at.
Mind the standing water. It teaches you medicine quickly.
I wonder what the mud does to a wound.
They can't be all savages. Probably. I'd like to check.
Stay together. I'd rather not dissect this in public.
Don't drink. Don't touch.
Metal and bone and dust. A scientist's dream and a patient's nightmare.
I'd love to look inside one of these machines.
Quiet. The ancients left a lot of notes here.
Nobles. Fickle. And I need a sponsor.
Do not mention my age. I am old enough.
Stay near. Slavers do not mind a medic.
Interesting. Quick, check them. For loot, I mean.
Done. I'll bandage the rest if anyone wants it.
They fall like patients, really.
Do not look at me like that. I am a medic first.
Hold still, I diagnose myself. Ow.
Don't panic. It's a manageable wound.
Get me my bag. Now.
Thanks. I'd have done it myself, but my hands shake.
You have good technique. Don't tell anyone I said so.
Fine. Back to work.
Do you know a noble who funds research? Not that I trust one.
I patch people. It's the least I can do.
Don't call me a child. I'm older than I look.
Not hiring, not selling, not interested. Unless you pay.
I keep my knives close and my opinions closer.
Realist, that's me. Fighting is for people who like losing teeth.
Need something patched? I charge less than the doctors.
I'd rather argue, but I'll cut you if I must.
Put the blade down. Think about your teeth.
You picked the wrong woman to bully.
Jewel is on the road, dry as bone and sharp as a razor. Not a fighter, but you won't like crossing her.
A Scorchlander woman named Jewel will patch you up and tell you what you did wrong.
Jewel doesn't boast and doesn't flinch.
Had an argument with Jewel over a bill once. I paid.
Hot, dry, and nobody smiling. Home.
Metal sun, metal ground. Mind your boots.
I know this sand. It doesn't forgive.
Wet and loud and everyone owes someone.
Keep the pack dry. Everything else can rot.
If it bites, I will tell you.
Empire city. Everything has a price and a tax.
Don't pay for a thing before you taste it.
Keep your hands where I can see them.
Not a dinner I'd sit down for.
I'll cook if we survive. Don't hold your breath.
The grass is too tall for my liking.
Done. Don't make a fuss.
I told them to think about their teeth.
Search them. They owe me for the trouble.
Practical. That's the whole trick.
Ow. That will cost somebody.
I am fine. Help me up, quietly.
I knew this would happen.
Thanks. I'll remember it. Not that I'll say so.
Careful. I bruise like fruit.
Good. Back on my feet.
I keep my distance from heroes. They don't live long.
Fighting costs more than it pays. Remember that.
I trust you a little. That's a lot.
Hands are my trade. Rope, nets, whatever wants mending.
If you need something fixed, ask. If you need a fight, ask someone else.
Things are slow. The family is stretched thin.
Don't mind me. I only carry a knife for fish.
I'm not looking for trouble. Don't make me find it.
Back off. I work with my hands and they're strong.
I have gutted bigger than you.
Soman from the fishing houses is looking for work. Strong hands, plain talk. Needs coin to settle some family business.
Her family is struggling. Soman will join you for the right price and not complain.
Quiet woman, good with her hands. Soman, they call her.
Soman needs thirty-five hundred cats. Sounds like a debt, not a dream.
Water I understand. This much of it, less so.
Good for fish. Bad for the knees.
Mind the edges. They are softer than they look.
Slow mud, slow water. Nets would rot in a day.
Smells like home, if home were worse.
Keep to the firm ground. I'll watch the rest.
Everything costs more here. Even the fish.
Nobody has time for a quiet woman.
Keep close and keep your purse.
Nothing grows here that I'd eat.
Be quiet. Be fast.
I'll carry what I can.
Plain work. Done.
Fish put up less of a fight.
Bind what you can. Take the rest.
I didn't enjoy that. Move on.
Ow. That will bruise.
I'm fine. Help me up.
I've taken worse from a net.
Thank you. I owe you a favour.
Plain work, that. Good.
Better. I can walk.
I need coin. Not much. Enough to tie up some loose ends.
Plain work, plain pay. That's all I ask.
I won't let you down. I never leave a job half done.
Don't step on the sprouts. They're all I have.
I am not a fighter. I like things that grow.
Is it safe ahead? Tell me honestly.
I keep a seed in my pocket.
Please don't hurt me. I'll give you what I have.
I do not want a fight.
Don't make me do this.
There is a nervous Scorchlander at the fishing houses with a pocket full of seeds. Green Finger, they call him. Gentle, jumpy.
Green Finger would sooner farm than fight. He will fight if cornered. Apologises afterwards.
A man who plants things in the Scorch. Brave, or daft.
Hire him if you want a quiet, skittish companion. He talks to the plants more than to you.
Green grass! Real grass. I could weep.
I miss soil that doesn't crack.
Look at the crops. Somebody knows what they're doing.
All this water, and nothing planted.
If the ground were firmer I'd settle here.
Is the water clean? Please say it's clean.
Please stay close. I'm scared.
Don't leave me behind. I'll carry things.
Those don't grow wild. Something tends them. That's worse.
Nothing grows here. Not a root. Not a spore.
I feel bad for the sand. It must be so dry.
I'll keep walking. I'm not stopping.
Oh. Oh no. That's awful.
Sorry. Sorry. Check them, please.
I didn't want that. Move on.
I will plant something where they fell. Later.
Ow! It hurts! Please help.
I'm sorry. I'm slow.
I'll get up. I will.
Thank you, thank you. You're so kind.
It does not hurt as much now.
I'll repay this. Somehow.
Do you think anything will ever grow properly in the Wend? I dream of it.
I'm afraid, but I'm here. That counts, right?
If we find good soil, can we stop? Just once?
Nothing new here. Nothing new anywhere.
I'd greet you properly, but what's the point.
I have talked to gurglers. They disappoint less than most.
If you want company, I'm available. I'm not good company.
Go on, then. Finish me. I have little else planned.
I'm already dead, more or less.
A fight. How novel. Come on.
There is a skeleton in Black Desert City so low-spirited it makes the others look cheerful. Sadneil.
Sadneil will join a party out of pure weakness, then complain at every step. Reliable in a gloomy way.
If a skeleton sighs at you, it's Sadneil.
Heard Sadneil say the gurglers were better company than people. He may be right.
Home. I'd say it's lovely, but I don't lie.
The sand is the same as ever. I wish I weren't.
I know every dune. None of them has helped.
Wet, cold, and noisy. Of course.
My joints rust in this air.
I suppose it's nice that something lives here.
They'll eat the flesh and leave the bones. Fine by me.
If they take me apart, I won't stop them.
I don't look appetising. That's the one bright spot.
Holy ground. I'm not welcome.
They hate us here. Honestly, fair enough.
Keep moving. Do not give them an excuse.
That's that. It changes nothing.
One more down. Another will come.
Search them. I won't enjoy it.
I should feel something. I don't.
Another crack. Another day.
I'm still here. Unfortunately.
Just leave me. No? Fine, help me.
Thank you. I'll be fine until the next time.
Don't bother with kindness. It won't take.
It helps a little. A little is enough.
Joining you was weakness, not choice. I regret nothing, because regret takes energy.
I've seen worse days. Not many.
If I stay quiet it isn't anger.
A retainer's life is long and dull.
Do you fight, stranger? Or just walk?
Peasant work kills a warrior's soul. Say it isn't so.
Pride, kin. Or not. I can't tell what you are.
At last, a fight worth having!
Draw. I've waited long for honest steel.
You won't leave. I won't allow it.
A Shek retainer called Oron hungers for battle. Would pay to be free of their lord. Thirty-five hundred cats, I heard.
Oron is bored. A bored Shek is a dangerous Shek. Hire them before they do something drastic.
There's a warrior in the Shek lands who wants a fight more than a meal. Oron. They would follow you into a pit.
Oron won't stay a peasant much longer. The question is who gets the sword.
Open sand. Open sky. This is where a Shek should walk.
A good place for a duel. A better place for a feast.
Pride, kin. I breathe easier here.
Cannibals. A fine test. Don't hold me back.
Many enemies, little honour. I'll take what I can.
Tall grass, wary eyes. This will be exciting.
Flatskins and their zealots. I'll wait to fight.
Their walls are high. My blade is long.
Don't draw yet. Soon.
Sun on my back and nothing to kill.
If anything dares cross us, I shall thank it.
Endless sand. Endless boredom.
That was a start. Show me more.
Honour to them. They died well.
Is that all? I'm only warmed up.
Pride, kin. Loot them.
A scratch. Give me a minute.
I have bled more for less.
Up. I'm not done.
I owe you. A Shek pays debts.
Good. Return me to the fight.
Your hands are steady. Well done.
I want a fight. Any fight. That is all.
Carry me into a battle worth singing about.
I won't abandon you. I don't abandon anyone.
If you're a slaver, say so now.
I escaped once. I won't be sold again.
Do you see any spiders? No? Good.
I charm my way out of most things.
I escaped the chains. I won't return.
Come close and find out what a slave learns.
Not today. Not ever. You will not take me.
There's an escaped slave with a removed brand and a bad temper. Miu. She screams at spiders long before they show.
Miu swears like a miner and fights like a fiend. Sells nothing. Buys nothing.
Her friend died to a spider, so I hear. Miu hasn't forgiven the whole species.
Miu hates the Holy Nation, the Empire and spiders. In that order, depending on the day.
Spiders! I hate spiders! Keep your eyes open!
Every shadow could be eight legs.
I swear, if one drops on me I'm burning this place down.
Home, roughly. Mud and mosquitoes and mad folk.
I know the bars here. Don't drink anything green.
Nobody asks questions in the swamp.
Empire land. The place is rife with slavers. Eyes up.
If anyone checks my wrist, I run.
I shouldn't be here. Let us leave.
Holy country. I like to charm my way out of problems.
Don't smile too much. Priests notice.
Say nothing. I mean it.
Hah! Fuck off back to the slaver who made you.
That's for every chain I ever wore.
Check them. They might have a key.
Nobody sells me, you bastards.
Shit! That stung.
I am up! Do not fuss.
Get me back in. Now.
Thanks. I'll remember. I always do.
Ow, careful. Fuck, that hurts.
Good. Back to it.
I was farm girl, then slave, then free.
Ask me about the spiders and I will talk for an hour.
I never forget a kindness. Or a chain.
Psst. Is the key near? No? Then keep walking.
Open air. I forgot how big it was.
I spent a lot of years behind bars. Don't stare.
Do not mention the Empire. Or do.
Another of Tengu's dogs. Come on.
I killed a lord once. Don't make me practice.
I lived in a cell. You won't put me back in one.
They say Luquin still lives in the Vault. Hold on to that if the Empire frightens you.
Luquin, the farmer's son who killed a lord. They made him write a tribute to Tengu..
The Anti-Slavers still sing about Luquin. Some believe it, some don't.
If you find the Vault, ask for the thin man with a wry mouth.
Last time I was here, they paraded me through the street.
I do not like these walls. Too many guards.
Keep your head low. Tengu has long arms.
Mud, reeds, no walls. Hah. Beautiful.
Breathe in. That's freedom, and it smells awful.
Nobody knows me here. Good.
Open. Open and bright. I could walk forever.
Nothing between me and the sky. I forgot what that was.
Did the dunes always look this large?
A cage is a cage, even a big one.
Eyes open. I won't be locked in again.
If they catch me, it won't be quick.
That's for every year I was held.
Tengu's men are weaker than they look.
Check them. They have keys.
Another bar closed forever.
I have survived worse in a cell.
Not this time. Up.
I won't die in the open.
Thank you. It's strange being kind to.
Right. Back to work.
I owe you. I don't forget.
I was in the Vault a long time. The air tastes strange now.
Thank you for opening the door.
If you fight the Empire, count me in.
Business, stranger? Make it quick, I'm off the clock.
A happy slave works harder. Remember that, if you ever buy.
Don't say slave lover. I don't like the word.
Everything has a price. The people too.
I'm a businessman. Don't make me waste a blade on you.
You're bad for trade. Therefore you die.
Take the slave and go. No? Pity.
Garret buys his slave a drink and calls it good business. Nobody in the bar is sure whether to laugh.
They called Garret a slave lover to his face once.
A dealer who pampers his stock. Garret. The Anti-Slavers hate the whole thing and him more.
Garret says a content slave is a profitable slave. Probably the nicest monster I know.
Business concluded.
Pity. I wanted to haggle.
The profit is in the stripping.
Always more at the end of a fight than the start.
I'm only the secretary. Nobody listens to me, so don't start.
The Emperor is busy. He is always busy. Do you have an appointment?
Speak quickly. My master dislikes waiting and so do I.
Don't bring up the nobles. I have to live with them.
Guards! Deal with this, please.
I'm a diplomat, not a swordsman. But I'll cut if I must.
The Empire doesn't forget its enemies, stranger.
A friend of the Empire. How rare.
Your name is known here. I won't say how.
Welcome. Don't overstay it.
Tengu has a tired little secretary named Koin. He decides who gets favours and who gets nothing.
Koin the diplomat smiles at everyone and trusts no one.
If you want an audience with the Emperor, Koin is the gatekeeper.
They say Koin corrects Tengu's pronunciation and survives. I'd pay to see that.
A diplomat's burden. Sorry about that.
I did warn them. In writing.
Please remove the bodies from the hall.
Another matter settled.
Please, sir, don't hurt me. I'm only here to help.
I'm a squire. Squires carry things.
I'm nervous around visitors. Forgive me.
Hello! May I interest you in a membership? Please say yes.
No, no, please! I'll fetch someone!
I'm only a squire! Don't hurt me!
Guards! Guards, please!
There's a Hive squire at the Traders Guild who flinches at his own shadow. Yamdu.
Yamdu handles membership enquiries and dreads every one. Kindly man.
The noble's squire fears everything but never fails to help.
If you meet the nervous drone at Trader's Edge, buy something.
I didn't want that! I'm so sorry!
Please look away. I'll clean up.
Is it over? It's over.
I won't sleep tonight.
Eyes on the grass. The cannibals are patient.
Keep clear of the post unless you have business.
I have hunted cannibals for years. Don't tell me they're gone.
Move along. This is no place for a stroll.
You aren't welcome here. Draw.
I've fought worse than you in the dark.
Don't test the Flotsam.
Friend of Flotsam. Welcome. Eyes open.
Good to see a friendly face on this road.
You have helped us. We remember.
The Flotsam guard at the scout post escaped a cannibal cage years ago. Mani. He doesn't joke about cannibals.
Mani trades what he can and kills cannibals when he must. Both with the same face.
Heard Mani lost his friends to a cannibal camp and walked out alone.
If you hurt Flotsam, Mani remembers. If you help, he remembers that too.
Cannibals don't stay dead. Remember that.
Down. Check the grass for more.
That's one less. Keep watching.
Burn them. Don't leave them to the plains.
Ells is hungry! Got food? Got rum?
Ells doesn't steal. Ells borrows.
The guards hit Ells. Ells doesn't like the guards.
Is it rum? Ells smells rum!
Ells will fight! Ells isn't a coward!
No bounty! Ells isn't worth it!
Ells doesn't want to! But will!
Ells the rum thief raided the distillery again. Daft as a post, but nobody can catch him.
Someone put a bounty on a half-wit named Ells. For stealing rum. The world is a strange place.
Ells talks about himself like a stranger. Sweet, in a sad way. Feed him and he follows you anywhere.
Barkeeps hate him, guards beat him, and he still comes back for rum. Ells.
Ells doesn't like this place.
Ells smells rum. Can Ells go look?
Ells will be good. Promise.
Mud! Ells likes mud. And rum.
Ells isn't scared. Ells is a little scared.
Is there rum in the swamp? Please say yes.
Ells doesn't like the tall grass.
Ells will stay close. Very close.
Don't leave Ells behind.
No rum here. Ells is sad.
Ells misses the distillery.
Ells will carry things, if there's food.
Ells did it! Eeheehee!
Ma said Ells would do good!
Ells is strong! Ells is strong!
Ells needs a drink now!
Ow! Ells is hurt!
Ells wants Ma!
Ells will get up. Ells will.
Ells thanks you kindly!
Ow, careful! But thank you!
Ells feels better. Ells is happy.
What are you in for? I'm in for something.
I don't hate you. Don't think I do.
You'll do. Maybe later.
Say something. Anything. The silence is worse.
I'll take my time. You won't enjoy it.
Come here. I'm very calm.
Choke on a cactus. Then I'll help you do it.
There's a man in Tengu's Vault who calmly says what he did. Psycho, he's called. Nobody says it twice.
Psycho sits in his cell and smiles. The guards stopped speaking to him.
Word is, a martial artist in the Vault is in for disembowelling. Matter-of-fact. That's the frightening part.
Psycho was framed, he insists. Then he tells you what he did anyway.
Done. That was easy.
I've done worse for less.
Keep still. This is the fun part.
Next.
Out. We must go out. Soon.
This isn't a good place.
Few words. Fewer hours. Move.
Hive doesn't belong in cages.
You keep us in. You die.
Hive won't be caged again.
We go out now.
A Hive worker in Tengu's Vault wants out so badly he stares at the door all day.
Espher speaks little and means all of it.
I heard a South Hive drone sits in the Vault and counts the guards' steps. Espher.
If the Vault falls, Espher will be the first through the door.
Done. Out now.
We leave. Quickly.
Free. Not yet. But closer.
No time. Go.
Pride, kin. Even in a cage a Shek has his pride.
Do you bring news or only a stare?
The Vault has been quiet for too long.
Stop looking at me. Say something.
I owe the Empire a blade.
A Shek bows to no cage.
You won't like the sound of my laughter.
A Shek called Sinklyde sits in Tengu's Vault with his pride intact. They haven't broken him yet.
Sinklyde has been behind those bars long enough to learn every guard's name.
A Shek in the Vault? Sinklyde. He will tell you honour is worth more than freedom. Then ask you to break him out.
The Vault holds a Shek who hums battle songs. Sinklyde. Guards complain.
Pride, kin. That's how a Shek fights.
They knew the risk.
Search them. Quickly.
A short fight. A shorter life.
AHHH! You! Come closer! No, go away!
They put me in here for screaming. I scream because they put me in here.
Quiet. Hush. No! Scream!
Do you hear it? No? I do.
AAAAHHH! Go away!
Get away from me! AAAH!
I'll scream until you leave!
Someone in Tengu's Vault never stops screaming. Screamy. Even the guards take their lunch elsewhere.
Screamy does nothing but scream. Nobody has asked why.
I heard you can hear Screamy from half a mile outside the Vault.
If a scream wakes you at night near the Vault, that's Screamy.
AAAAH!
Hush now! Hush!
Quiet, quiet, quiet!
No more! No more!
I lead a caravan. If you aren't buying, don't block the road.
Free Traders go where the cats are. Keep out of our way.
Mind your hands near my cart.
I don't talk to men with swords unless they pay.
Bandit or fool. Either way, you pay.
My caravan has survived worse than you.
I escaped chains once. I won't fear you.
A friend of the Free Traders. Good. We need more.
You have my thanks. Truly.
Safe roads, friend. Hard to come by.
Harmothoe leads the Free Traders. Wealthy in cats, ruthless with thieves.
They sing about Harmothoe in the Free Trader camps. Not a gentle song.
A caravan leader who killed her old masters. Harmothoe. Keep your hands clean when you deal with her.
Harmothoe pays in coin and holds grudges in iron.
Pay your debts, or the road will.
Free Traders don't forgive.
Loot them. Quickly, before dark.
That's how we protect cats.
Flotsam sees everything. Walk carefully.
You look battle ready. But you aren't one of us.
State your business or move on.
I carry a blade for a reason. Remember that.
Another fool for Flotsam to bury.
Leave. Or learn why we're feared.
I train with steel. Come and meet it.
A friend of Flotsam is a friend of mine.
We remember our friends. We remember the rest too.
Good fighting. Keep it up.
Yayoi trains the newer ninjas. Hard on them, fair on the sword.
People say Yayoi fights better than most Flotsam veterans. Few challenge her.
Yayoi walks without a sound. You only notice when it's too late.
Paladins fear Flotsam, and Yayoi is the reason.
Flotsam doesn't lose.
Quiet. Efficient. Done.
Search them. Leave the rest.
Too slow. They always are.
Do you carry a wanted poster? Because I'm it.
Drought wasn't my fault. Say otherwise and bleed.
Leave me be. I answer to no one.
I deserted my duties. I regret nothing.
Another bounty hunter. Come and try.
I don't care what the poster says.
You won't take me alive.
White Eyebrow abandoned his duties and now they blame him for the Brown Drought.
Nobody believes one man could cause a drought. Nobody except the clan he left.
White Eyebrow has a camp somewhere in the sands. Wanted. Dangerous.
If the poster is true, he's a menace. If false, he's a scapegoat.
Another hunter down.
The poster lies. The blade doesn't.
Search them. They carry coin.
Nobody takes me.
